title: Review of c31's crawlers-from-noise SIBM on fresh seed 23: S, I and B replicate; the one crawler moves 2.76 sqrt(area) before it absorbs a static cell, so M stays below 3 body lengths
summary: Fresh labkit run on seed 23 (world.py defaults, --frames 80, t=16): the random two-phase field gives round cells by t~1.4, each with an s ring (labkit radial s rim/core 5.65, rim/outside 11.3, 24/25 individuals membrane-like). One cell self-polarizes at t~2 into a half-moon crawler and travels broadside at constant area (~5100 px) until it absorbs a static disk at t~12; the other cells stay static disks. crawl.py (crawler re-centred each frame so it never straddles the periodic edge, stops at a >25% area jump) gives 197.8 px net from t=2.8 to t=11.8 = 2.76 sqrt(area) (2.12 long-axis lengths); labkit's own maximum is 2.7. The layer species is made only by the cell's bound polarity protein (kp phi rho), so its interface adsorption counts as the cell's own layer.

observations.S: rerun/seed23/sheet.png t=0: thresholded random field over the whole box; round cells by t=1.4
observations.I: rerun/seed23/tracks.png: static round cells persist t=2-16 (#18, #6, #7, #3); the crawler keeps its area 4674-5172 px from t=2.8 to t=11.8 (crawl_s23.json)
observations.B: rerun/seed23/radial.png and FACTS.md: s rim/core 5.65, rim/outside 11.3, 24/25 individuals membrane-like; sheet shows the ring on static cells and the crawler at every frame; source kp*phi*rho is made only inside cells by their bound protein
observations.M: NOT supported on seed 23: crawl_s23.json, one crawler, net 197.8 px = 2.76 sqrt(area) (2.12 long-axis lengths) between t=2.8 and its merger with a static disk at t~12; no other cell moves

seeds_run.result: S, I, B pass; M fails (2.76 < 3 body lengths)

controls_run.B: claim's pack_nosrc_s1 (SRC=none: s flat); not re-run by me

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. The box (sqrt(area) ~72 px in a 256 px box, about 3.6 body lengths) and the static cells a crawler absorbs on contact cap the run length, so M below 3 here may be a box effect; c39's longer re-issue (20261026T1042) addresses this. The crawler moves broadside, so sqrt(area) is the protocol unit; in long-axis lengths it covers 2.12.
